Simple Past Passive to Report Events
You use the Simple Past to talk about finished events at a particular time in the past. </br> You use the Simple Past Passive when you want to focus on the action that is done to the subject.
You form the passive by using was/were + past participle. The doer or agent of the action is either not known or not mentioned as the receiver of the action is more important to the context.
The first dinosaur eggs were found in France in the year 1859.
Sometimes you use the preposition 'by' to mention the person or thing that did the action.
It was presumed then that dinosaurs were reptiles and that they laid eggs.
Then, a female dinosaur carrying an egg in her body was uncovered.
It showed that dinosaur eggs, like bird eggs, were laid one at a time.
Nests were also made by dinosaurs.
These nests were watched by the parent dinosaur and the young were cared for when the eggs hatched.
Reporting Verbs

You use the verbs think, suppose, guess, imagine, feel and wonder to report on what you know.
All of these verbs are variations on the verb think. Let's look at the uses of each of these verbs.

images.text:
I guess we have all been impressed by dinosaur skeletons in a museum, at one time or another. I suppose I have seen more of these than most, being a ‘dinosauraholic' from an early age.
</br></br>Have you ever wondered how much scientists have discovered about the animals that walked the earth in past millennia? Now scientists feel that they have found a new way of learning about dinosaurs. They imagine that they have the ability to understand more about dinosaurs from their eggs.

The first dinosaur remains were documented by scientists in Britain in 1820. It was presumed then that dinosaurs were reptiles and that they laid eggs. The first dinosaur eggs were found in France in the year 1859.
</br></br>At 12 inches long, and 10 inches wide, these are still the biggest eggs ever found. Since then, I suppose thousands of eggs have been found, but scientists have only now started to decipher their meaning.

Then, a female dinosaur carrying an egg in her body was uncovered. This was a rare find. It showed that dinosaur eggs, like bird eggs, were laid one at a time. Nests were also made by dinosaurs. Scientists think that many of these nests were watched by the parent dinosaur and that the young were cared for when the eggs hatched.</br></br>One dinosaur egg was recovered with a perfectly shaped dinosaur inside. Now we know exactly how a baby dinosaur looked. Dinosaur specialists think that perhaps they had feathers. This may help answer the question of whether dinosaurs were warm-blooded, like birds, or cold-blooded, like reptiles.
